thread.title: Nvidia, Top Tech Stocks Lead As S&P Bounces Off Key Support Line

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Nvidia, Top Tech Stocks Lead As S&P Bounces Off Key Support Line

organizations.name: top tech stocks lead as s&p

text:
The stock market didn't let up on volatility Friday, leaving key index ETFs vacillating between red and black throughout the session. They were mixed in late-afternoon trading.
Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Intel ( INTC ) boosted the Dow Jones industrials Friday as techs led the rebound from Thursday's sell-off. Nvidia ( NVDA ) soared on earnings.
X PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) rose 0.9%, SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) advanced 0.8% and SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) added 0.5%. Emerging markets also led, with iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ( EEM ) up 0.9%. The S&P 500 index fell to its 200-day line but found support and rebounded.
Big-cap techs advanced in the blue chip index: Microsoft was up 2.5%, Intel 1.9% and Cisco ( CSCO ) 1.3%. Apple ( AAPL ), which has been in both positive and negative territory today, held a fractional gain%. Microsoft recovered its 50-day moving average; Apple is still below its 200-day line.
Semiconductor, technology and banks were among the biggest sector-fund gainers in the stock market today . VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ( SMH ) and iShares PHLX Semiconductor ( SOXX ) reversed from earlier losses to advance 2% each. Nvidia surged 7% on a big earnings and sales beat. The graphics-chip designer raised guidance for the current quarter.
Gold, energy and consumer staples lagged. Oil and gold plays slipped along with their underlying commodity prices. VanEck Vectors Junior Gold Miners ( GDXJ ) and VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ( GDX ) tumbled 2.9% and 2.4%, respectively. PowerShares DB Energy ( DBE ) slid 2%, on track for a sixth straight decline as it dropped further below its 50-day line.
High-Octane Play It's tough to find rising ETFs when the stock market takes such a nasty tumble like it did on Thursday. But a handful of leveraged inverse funds scored.
Leveraged funds are not for the faint of heart, or even for most retail investors. They can jump sharply when a major index is up, but can crash hard when the opposite occurs. Likewise, leveraged inverse funds tend to soar when the index they track sinks. They are not intended to be a long-term play.
ProShares Ultra Short QQQ ( SQQQ ) vaulted nearly 13% Thursday as the Nasdaq 100 index dropped more than 4%. The $455.5 million fund, which aims to provide three times the inverse of the Nasdaq 100's daily performance, has been mired in a steep descent since its February 2010 launch. After all, the bull market is entering its ninth year.
However, the ETF perked up 12% on Monday, as the broader market stumbled. SQQQ regained its 50-day moving average for the first time since late September. It fell back below the support line on Tuesday, and reclaimed it Thursday.
Its year-to-date return of 1.2% through Feb. 8 was ahead of the S&P 500's nearly flat advance on that date. The ETF's long-term performance track record leaves much to be desired, with average annual losses of more than 40% over the past three and five years. SQQQ bears a 0.95% expense ratio.
